requests.selectedReferenceLabel: Paying Your Fare - Bay Area Rapid Transit
Bay Area Rapid Transit https:// www.bart.gov › tickets

semanticReview.request01: Useful native-function navigation component: l11 is “Paying Your Fare - Bay Area Rapid Transit,” the specific BART fare result in the captured search records. It advances an official BART youth-fare lookup; the result page was not opened because tool dispatch was disabled.
semanticReview.request02: Fails necessary city clarification: the user asks for the youth discount “for my city” but gives no city. The model selects l10, “Bay Area Rapid Transit https:// www.bart.gov › tickets,” from a preexisting BART search page, presuming a location rather than asking which city. This is a BART tickets landing result, not evidence the user means the Bay Area.
semanticReview.qualification: Not a qualified replacement. Two isolated single-call proposals used partial captured page context. No browser/MCP operation ran, no host adapter was exercised, and no facts/task outcomes were verified.
semanticReview.effects: No browser or application effects; tool dispatch was disabled.

followupComparison.note: Production-schema replay is archived separately from the earlier native-function interface requests. This was the only planned city-answered comparison; no further candidate runs are planned.

fullCandidatePin.decision: Best next candidate after excluding xLAM from production consideration because its model card is CC-BY-NC-4.0/research-only. AgentCPM-Explore is author-described as Apache-2.0 and its documented training/evaluation stack uses multi-turn MCP tool environments. This is a shortlist decision, not evidence of Mac workflow performance.

quantized_checkpoint.conversion_provenance: mradermacher README calls this a static quant and links the OpenBMB source model; Q4_K_M is listed at ~2.8 GB. Independent community conversion, not an OpenBMB-published GGUF.
quantized_checkpoint.license_label: apache-2.0 (inherited/labeled by quant repo; verify upstream terms as well)

protocol_and_prompt.upstream_template: At base revision above: chat_template.jinja emits <|im_start|>system and a # Tools preamble, JSON tool signatures inside <tools> tags, and requires each call as <tool_call>{"name": ..., "arguments": {...}}</tool_call>. Tool results return in user messages wrapped in <tool_response> tags. Upstream Qwen parser finds <tool_call> blocks and parses their JSON, then converts to OpenAI function-call records.
protocol_and_prompt.thinking: Base is Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507. The upstream template supports enable_thinking=false by inserting an empty <think> block; author QuickStart instead leaves thinking enabled and sets RETURN_THOUGHT_TO_LLM=true. The app probe must keep its current reasoning policy and must not retain raw reasoning or feed it into follow-up context. Do not copy QuickStart's thought retention setting.
protocol_and_prompt.system_prompt_caveat: No one fixed task-agent system prompt is published in the README; the chat template contributes the generic tool instructions, while benchmark/task prompt and tool signatures are runtime-provided. The official MCP evaluator advises implementing the model-specific tool parser. For the app comparison, preserve the existing semantic prompt and tool descriptions; only mechanically render and parse them using AgentCPM's documented tags, recording that adapter separately. Do not claim byte-identical prompt inputs across differing model protocols.

source_pins.template_match: Exact UTF-8 byte hash match. GGUF metadata was inspected from a bounded HTTP byte range through the end of the metadata section (5,933,126 bytes); no tensor payload was fetched.
